title: AVO-1 – Module 3, 4
description: Final exam covering transformers, AC and DC circuits, filters, measuring instruments, oscilloscopes, three-phase systems, resonance, and basic electrical measurements.

questions.question: What type of transformer core is commonly used for high-frequency transformers?
questions.explanation: Air-core transformers are commonly used at high frequencies because conventional iron cores have increased core losses at high frequencies.

questions.question: In a series RC circuit, the total current I —
options: C. Is always in phase with the source voltage
questions.explanation: In a capacitive RC circuit, the current leads the applied voltage by a phase angle.

questions.question: Resistance is measured using a —
questions.explanation: An ohmmeter is designed to measure electrical resistance in ohms.

questions.question: How is energy transferred from the primary winding to the secondary winding of a transformer?
questions.explanation: A transformer transfers energy through the changing magnetic flux linking the primary and secondary windings.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT generally true about passive filters?
options: A. They are easier to design
B. They require an external power supply for gain
C. They can be made using resistors, capacitors, and inductors
questions.explanation: No explanation.

questions.question: A low-pass filter is designed to —
options: A. Pass high frequencies and block low frequencies
B. Block high frequencies while allowing low frequencies to pass
questions.explanation: A low-pass filter allows frequencies below its cutoff frequency to pass and attenuates higher frequencies.

questions.question: A transformer winding having a high number of turns is generally the —
questions.explanation: For a transformer, induced voltage is proportional to the number of turns, so the higher-voltage winding normally has more turns.

questions.question: What type of transformer has an output voltage higher than its input voltage?
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer increases the secondary voltage above the primary voltage.

questions.question: In a pure resistive AC circuit, current and voltage are —
questions.explanation: A pure resistance causes no phase shift, so current and voltage are in phase.

questions.question: RMS value of an AC voltage or current represents its —
options: A. Effective heating value compared with DC
C. Average value over one half-cycle only
questions.explanation: The RMS value is the effective value of an AC quantity and produces the same heating effect in a resistor as the equivalent DC value.

questions.question: What is meant by instantaneous voltage?
options: A. The voltage value at any particular instant of time
B. The maximum voltage of a complete cycle
C. The average voltage of all cycles
questions.explanation: Instantaneous voltage is the value of the voltage at a specific point in time.

questions.question: A transformer has 110 primary turns and 20 secondary turns. What is the primary-to-secondary turns ratio?
questions.explanation: The turns ratio is Np/Ns = 110/20 = 5.5, so the primary-to-secondary ratio is 5.5:1.

questions.question: An ammeter is connected —
options: A. In parallel with the circuit
B. In series with the circuit
C. Across the power supply only
questions.explanation: An ammeter must be connected in series so the circuit current flows through the meter.

questions.question: Multimeter sensitivity is commonly expressed in —
questions.explanation: Analog voltmeter sensitivity is commonly specified in ohms per volt, often expressed as kΩ/V.

questions.question: Which device is used to convert AC into DC?
questions.explanation: A rectifier converts alternating current into pulsating direct current, which can then be filtered for smoother DC.

questions.question: Which meter movement type uses magnetic repulsion as part of its operating principle?
questions.explanation: Moving-iron instruments can operate using the attraction or repulsion of magnetized iron parts.

questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure very high resistance values?
questions.explanation: A megohmmeter, often called a megger, is designed to measure very high insulation resistance.

questions.question: To measure voltage drop across a component, the meter should be connected —
options: A. In series with the component
B. In parallel with the component
C. In series with the power source only
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures potential difference between two points, so it is connected in parallel with the component.

questions.question: An oscilloscope primarily represents a signal as —
questions.explanation: An oscilloscope displays the variation of an electrical signal, commonly voltage, with time.

questions.question: Which statement is true for a parallel circuit?
options: A. The current in each branch is less than the total current
B. The same current always flows through every branch
C. The total current is less than every branch current
questions.explanation: In a parallel circuit, total current is the sum of the branch currents, so each individual branch current is normally less than the total.

questions.question: The impedance of a series RLC circuit at resonance is —
questions.explanation: At series resonance, inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, leaving only resistance; therefore impedance is minimum.

questions.question: A filter made using resistors, capacitors, and/or inductors without active devices is called a —
questions.explanation: Passive filters use passive components such as resistors, capacitors, and inductors and do not provide power gain.

questions.question: Which expression can be used to calculate power factor in an AC circuit?
questions.explanation: Power factor is PF = P/S, where P is true power in watts and S is apparent power in volt-amperes.

questions.question: In a three-phase delta connection, the —
options: A. Line voltage is equal to phase voltage
B. Line voltage is √3 times phase voltage
C. Line voltage is half the phase voltage
questions.explanation: For a balanced delta connection, line voltage equals phase voltage.

questions.question: A signal that does not change with time is a —
questions.explanation: A constant signal has a fixed value with time and is therefore a DC signal.

questions.question: A transformer has 1000 primary turns and is connected to 250 V AC. If the required secondary voltage is 400 V, how many secondary turns are required?
questions.explanation: Using Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, Ns = (400/250) × 1000 = 1,600 turns.

questions.question: In each complete cycle of an AC sine wave, how many maximum peak values occur?
questions.explanation: A complete sine-wave cycle has one positive maximum peak and one negative maximum peak, giving two maximum peak values in magnitude.

questions.question: Values measured at any particular instant along an AC waveform are called —
questions.explanation: An instantaneous value is the magnitude of an AC quantity at a particular instant of time.

questions.question: The total opposition to AC current flow in a circuit is called —
questions.explanation: Impedance is the total opposition to AC current and includes both resistance and reactance.

questions.question: Which waveform rises upward and then drops sharply?
questions.explanation: A saw-tooth waveform has a gradual rise or fall followed by a sharp transition back to the starting level.

questions.question: The condition in an RLC circuit where inductive and capacitive reactances are equal and opposite is called —
questions.explanation: At resonance, XL and XC are equal in magnitude and opposite in phase, so they cancel.

questions.question: If the capacitance in a series RLC circuit is decreased while inductance remains constant, the resonant frequency —
questions.explanation: The resonant frequency is fr = 1/(2π√LC). Decreasing capacitance increases the resonant frequency.

questions.question: What is the relationship between current and voltage in a pure resistive AC circuit?
options: C. Current is in phase with voltage
questions.explanation: In a pure resistive circuit, current and voltage reach their corresponding maximum and zero values at the same time.

questions.question: Which statement describes an ideal transformer?
options: A. It has no losses and no magnetic leakage
B. It has high copper losses
C. It always has a voltage drop due to resistance
questions.explanation: An ideal transformer is assumed to have no power losses and perfect magnetic coupling with no leakage flux.

questions.question: Filters created using transistors or other active devices are called —
questions.explanation: Active filters use active components such as transistors or operational amplifiers along with passive components.

questions.question: In an ideal transformer, if the number of secondary turns is tripled while the load condition is considered through the turns relationship, the secondary current will —
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, voltage and current ratios are inversely related to turns. Increasing secondary turns by three times causes the corresponding secondary current rating to decrease to one-third.

questions.question: Which statement about an ammeter is NOT correct?
options: A. It is connected in series
B. It should have very low internal resistance
C. It is connected across the source voltage
questions.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series with the load, not directly across a voltage source.

questions.question: In a three-phase delta connection, the —
options: A. Line voltage equals phase voltage
B. Line current always equals phase current
C. Line voltage is √3 times phase voltage
questions.explanation: In a balanced delta connection, line voltage is equal to phase voltage.

questions.question: Which meter movement is generally not suitable for directly measuring AC?
questions.explanation: A D'Arsonval moving-coil movement responds to the average direction of current and therefore requires rectification to measure AC.

questions.question: A D'Arsonval meter movement converts —
options: B. Electrical energy into mechanical movement
C. Chemical energy into electrical energy
questions.explanation: Current through the moving coil produces a magnetic force that creates mechanical movement of the pointer.

questions.question: Which oscilloscope control moves the traced image up or down on the screen?
questions.explanation: The vertical position control moves the displayed waveform upward or downward on the screen.

questions.question: Which oscilloscope control adjusts the electron beam so the displayed trace is sharply defined?
questions.explanation: The focus control adjusts the electron beam to produce a sharp, clearly defined trace.

questions.question: A common fault in an inductor is —
options: C. Perfect continuity with no winding
questions.explanation: A broken winding or connection can cause an inductor to have an open circuit.

questions.question: In a three-phase star/wye connection, the —
options: A. Line current and phase current are the same
B. Line voltage and phase voltage are always the same
C. Line current is √3 times phase current
questions.explanation: For a balanced star connection, line current is equal to phase current.

questions.question: Why are transformer cores laminated?
questions.explanation: Thin insulated laminations increase the resistance to circulating eddy currents and therefore reduce eddy-current losses.

questions.question: In a balanced three-phase star/wye connection, the line voltage is —
options: C. One-third of the phase voltage
questions.explanation: For a balanced star connection, VL = √3 VP.

questions.question: An oscilloscope can be used to represent a signal's —
questions.explanation: The oscilloscope commonly displays voltage amplitude as a function of time, allowing waveform frequency and other characteristics to be observed.

questions.question: Why are electrical systems and equipment grounded?
questions.explanation: Grounding provides a safe path for fault current and helps protect people and equipment from electric shock and damage.

questions.question: In a balanced three-phase delta connection, the magnitude of line current is —
questions.explanation: For a balanced delta connection, IL = √3 IP.

questions.question: A digital multimeter can typically measure —
options: A. AC/DC voltage, AC/DC current, and resistance
questions.explanation: A typical digital multimeter provides measurements such as AC/DC voltage, AC/DC current, and resistance.

questions.question: If the period of an AC waveform is 25 ms, what is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is f = 1/T. With T = 25 ms = 0.025 s, f = 1/0.025 = 40 Hz.

questions.question: Which statement about apparent power and true power is generally correct for an AC circuit?
options: A. Apparent power is always less than true power
B. Apparent power is equal to reactive power only
C. Apparent power is equal to or greater than true power
questions.explanation: Apparent power S is the vector combination of true and reactive power, so its magnitude is equal to or greater than true power P.

questions.question: The peak value of a sinusoidal AC quantity is approximately —
questions.explanation: For a sine wave, RMS = peak/√2, so peak = 1.414 × RMS.
